# wallix.bastion.timeframe

Manage timeframes on a WALLIX Bastion — module

*Added in version 1.0.0 of `wallix.bastion`.*

## Synopsis

- Create, update or delete a timeframe on a WALLIX Bastion.
- A timeframe is a set of periods during which users, groups or authorizations are allowed.
- Equivalent of the `wallix-bastion_timeframe` Terraform resource.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Comments |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="parameter-api-version"></a>**api_version** | `str` | Version of the Bastion REST API to use, `v3.8` or `v3.12`.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_API_VERSION` environment variable is used, then `v3.12`. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-host"></a>**bastion_host** | `str` | Hostname or IP address of the WALLIX Bastion.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_HOST` environment variable is used. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-password"></a>**bastion_password** | `str` | Password of [`bastion_user`](#parameter-bastion-user).<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_PASSWORD` environment variable is used.<br>One of [`bastion_password`](#parameter-bastion-password) or [`bastion_token`](#parameter-bastion-token) is required. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-port"></a>**bastion_port** | `int` | HTTPS port of the WALLIX Bastion API.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_PORT` environment variable is used, then `443`. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-timeout"></a>**bastion_timeout** | `int` | Timeout in seconds of each HTTP request to the Bastion API.<br><br>Default: `30` |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-token"></a>**bastion_token** | `str` | API key of [`bastion_user`](#parameter-bastion-user). Takes precedence over [`bastion_password`](#parameter-bastion-password).<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_TOKEN` environment variable is used. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-user"></a>**bastion_user** | `str` | User to authenticate with. With [`bastion_token`](#parameter-bastion-token), the user the API key belongs to.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_USER` environment variable is used. |
| <a id="parameter-csrf-enabled"></a>**csrf_enabled** | `bool` | Send the CSRF token the Bastion issues at login (Bastion 12.0.3 and later).<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_CSRF_ENABLED` environment variable is used, then `true`. |
| <a id="parameter-description"></a>**description** | `str` | Description of the timeframe. |
| <a id="parameter-is-overtimable"></a>**is_overtimable** | `bool` | Whether sessions may go on after the end of the timeframe. |
| <a id="parameter-periods"></a>**periods** | `list / elements=dict` | Periods of the timeframe. Order does not matter, neither does the order of [`periods[].week_days`](#parameter-periods-week-days).<br>When set, replaces all the periods of the timeframe. Use `[]` to remove all periods.<br>Two identical periods are refused by the Bastion. |
| <a id="parameter-periods-end-date"></a>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;↳ **end_date** | `str` / required | Last day of the period, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. |
| <a id="parameter-periods-end-time"></a>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;↳ **end_time** | `str` / required | End of the daily time slot, as `hh:mm`. Must be after [`periods[].start_time`](#parameter-periods-start-time), or `00:00` for the end of the day. |
| <a id="parameter-periods-start-date"></a>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;↳ **start_date** | `str` / required | First day of the period, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. |
| <a id="parameter-periods-start-time"></a>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;↳ **start_time** | `str` / required | Start of the daily time slot, as `hh:mm`. |
| <a id="parameter-periods-week-days"></a>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;↳ **week_days** | `list / elements=str` / required | Days of the week the time slot applies to. At least one is required.<br><br>Choices: `monday`, `tuesday`, `wednesday`, `thursday`, `friday`, `saturday`, `sunday` |
| <a id="parameter-state"></a>**state** | `str` | Whether the timeframe should exist.<br><br>Choices: `present` (default), `absent` |
| <a id="parameter-timeframe-name"></a>**timeframe_name** | `str` / required | Name of the timeframe. Identifies the timeframe on the Bastion. |
| <a id="parameter-validate-certs"></a>**validate_certs** | `bool` | Whether to validate the Bastion's TLS certificate.<br>Only disable this for test instances with self-signed certificates.<br>If not set, `WALLIX_BASTION_VALIDATE_CERTS` is used, then the inverse of `WALLIX_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY`, then `true`. |

## Attributes

| Attribute | Support | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **check_mode** | full | Can run in check_mode and return changed status prediction without modifying target. |
| **diff_mode** | full | Will return details on what has changed (or possibly needs changing in check_mode), when in diff mode. |

## Notes

- Options left unset keep their current value on the Bastion.
- Do not manage the built-in `allthetime` timeframe with this module.
- The environment variables are the ones of the `wallix/wallix-bastion` Terraform provider, so one shell configuration serves both tools.
- Set the connection options once per play with `module_defaults` and the `group/wallix.bastion.bastion` action group.
- These modules call the Bastion API from the host they run on; use them with `delegate_to` or on a play targeting `localhost`.

## Examples

```yaml
- name: Allow access during office hours in 2026
  wallix.bastion.timeframe:
    timeframe_name: office-hours
    description: Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 18:00
    periods:
      - start_date: "2026-01-01"
        end_date: "2026-12-31"
        start_time: "08:00"
        end_time: "18:00"
        week_days: [monday, tuesday, wednesday, thursday, friday]

- name: Remove a timeframe
  wallix.bastion.timeframe:
    timeframe_name: office-hours
    state: absent
```

## Return values

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="return-changed-fields"></a>**changed_fields** | `list / elements=str` | Options that differed from the Bastion and were updated.<br><br>Returned: when the timeframe already existed and [`state=present`](#parameter-state)<br><br>Sample: `["periods"]` |
| <a id="return-timeframe"></a>**timeframe** | `dict` | The timeframe as returned by the Bastion API after the change.<br>In check mode, the expected timeframe. `null` when [`state=absent`](#parameter-state).<br><br>Returned: always<br><br>Sample: see [below](#sample-timeframe) |

<a id="sample-timeframe"></a>

### Sample of `timeframe`

```yaml
description: Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 18:00
id: 1a0f6daa9f92d6b9005056b66c8b
is_overtimable: false
periods:
- end_date: '2026-12-31'
  end_time: '18:00'
  start_date: '2026-01-01'
  start_time: 08:00
  week_days:
  - monday
  - tuesday
  - wednesday
  - thursday
  - friday
timeframe_name: office-hours
url: https://bastion.example.com/api/v3.12/timeframes/1a0f6daa9f92d6b9005056b66c8b
```
